subject: Biology
description: Digestive enzymes, organs (mouth, stomach, intestine, liver), absorption

questions.stem: DIGESTION OF STARCH begins in the:
questions.explanation: MOUTH — saliva contains AMYLASE (PTYALIN — secreted by salivary glands). Breaks STARCH → MALTOSE (a disaccharide). Why chewing rice for long becomes sweet: more starch → maltose conversion. Also MUCIN (mucus, helps swallow), LYSOZYME (kills bacteria), water (liquefies food). pH ~6.8 (slightly acidic). STOMACH: HCl (pH 1.5-3.5) + PEPSIN (protein digestion); INACTIVATES salivary amylase. SMALL INTESTINE — main digestion + absorption site (pancreatic amylase, lipase, trypsin; bile from liver emulsifies fats). INSIGHT — digestion is a SEQUENCE: each organ contributes; output of one = input of next.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.stem: BILE, which emulsifies fats during digestion, is produced by the:
questions.explanation: LIVER produces BILE; STORED in GALLBLADDER (concentrated 5-10×); RELEASED into duodenum after meals via common bile duct. CONTAINS: bile SALTS (emulsify fats — break large fat globules into tiny droplets, increasing surface area for enzyme action — like detergent on greasy plate); BILIRUBIN (yellow waste from RBC breakdown — gives bile, urine, faeces colour); cholesterol; phospholipids. NO digestive enzymes itself. JAUNDICE = high bilirubin (yellow skin/eyes — liver/bile duct issue). GALLSTONES = cholesterol crystals; can block bile duct (very painful). LIVER — also detoxifies drugs/alcohol, makes plasma proteins, stores glycogen + iron + Vit A,D,B12.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.stem: Most ABSORPTION of digested nutrients occurs in the:
questions.explanation: SMALL INTESTINE — main digestion + absorption site. ~6 m long; 3 parts: DUODENUM (1st 25 cm — receives bile + pancreatic juice); JEJUNUM (~2.5 m); ILEUM (~3.5 m). VAST surface area: lined with VILLI (finger-like projections) + MICROVILLI (cell-membrane projections). Total surface area ~250 m² (= a tennis court!). Absorbed nutrients enter blood (via villi capillaries) or LYMPH (fats — via lacteals). LARGE INTESTINE: mainly absorbs WATER + electrolytes from undigested residue; gut bacteria produce some VIT K + B vitamins. Length ~1.5 m; ends at rectum + anus.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.stem: PANCREAS produces digestive enzymes AND a hormone for blood-sugar control. The hormone is:
questions.explanation: PANCREAS — both EXOCRINE (digestive enzymes via duct: amylase, lipase, trypsin → small intestine) + ENDOCRINE (hormones direct to blood). Endocrine cells = ISLETS OF LANGERHANS (named after the discoverer). BETA cells → INSULIN (lowers blood sugar; takes glucose into cells). ALPHA cells → GLUCAGON (raises blood sugar; opposite effect). DIABETES MELLITUS: TYPE 1 (autoimmune destruction of beta cells; need insulin shots; ~10% of cases); TYPE 2 (insulin resistance, often lifestyle-linked; ~90% of cases). India = 'DIABETES CAPITAL' (~80M cases). Insulin discovered by Banting + Best (1921, Nobel 1923) — saved millions of lives.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.stem: PEPSIN, the protein-digesting enzyme of the stomach, works best at:
questions.explanation: PEPSIN — protein-cutting enzyme; secreted by stomach's CHIEF CELLS as inactive PEPSINOGEN, activated by HCl (parietal cells secrete HCl) at low pH. Optimum pH ~1.5-2.0 (very acidic). HCl also: kills ingested bacteria, denatures proteins (unfolds them, exposing peptide bonds for pepsin). When food enters small intestine, pH rises (alkaline due to bile + pancreatic bicarbonate) → pepsin INACTIVATED. Other proteases: TRYPSIN + CHYMOTRYPSIN (small intestine, alkaline pH ~8). INSIGHT — enzymes have OPTIMUM pH + temperature; outside range, denature + lose function. Stomach pH naturally low to favour pepsin + sterilise food.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.stem: VILLI in the small intestine increase the:
questions.explanation: VILLI (singular: villus) — millions of tiny FINGER-LIKE projections on the inner wall of small intestine. Each villus has further MICROVILLI on its surface cells (BRUSH BORDER). Together they multiply absorption SURFACE AREA from a smooth-tube ~0.4 m² to ~250 m². Each villus contains: BLOOD CAPILLARIES (absorb glucose, amino acids, water-soluble vitamins, minerals); LACTEAL — central lymphatic vessel (absorbs digested fats + fat-soluble vitamins). NUTRIENTS go via blood to LIVER first (portal vein) for processing. INSIGHT — surface area is critical in biology: lungs (alveoli), kidneys (nephron tubules), brain (cortical folds), leaves (broad shape). Same evolutionary pressure across organs.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.stem: What is the LARGEST gland in the human body?
questions.explanation: LIVER — largest GLAND + largest INTERNAL ORGAN in human body. Adult ~1.5 kg (~2.5% of body weight). Lobes: right (larger) + left + 2 smaller. Functions (>500 known): bile production; metabolism of carbs (glycogen storage), proteins (urea synthesis), fats (cholesterol, lipoproteins); detoxification of alcohol + drugs + toxins; storage (glycogen, iron, Vit A, D, K, B12); plasma protein synthesis (albumin, clotting factors); immune (Kupffer cells filter blood). Has dual blood supply: hepatic artery (oxygenated) + portal vein (nutrient-rich from gut). Can REGENERATE — even after 75% removal! Liver diseases: HEPATITIS (A, B, C, D, E), CIRRHOSIS (alcohol/Hep), fatty liver.
